extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and USPTO disciplinary audiences
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order describing an individual practitioner's violations of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and the sanctions, conditions for reinstatement, reporting, and compliance procedures imposed by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — act with reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint Legal Conclusions found violations by (i) failing to file the '516 application in a timely fashion after telling clients he would file ASAP, and (ii) failing to file the '090 application in a timely fashion. Example of breach: promising filing by a date or time frame and not filing, causing client harm or misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — keep clients reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall keep clients reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations identified where respondent failed to inform clients that applications had not been filed when he had said they were filed, and misreported actual filing dates (e.g., claiming December filing when actual filing was July). Practical implication: timely, accurate disclosure of filing status, receipts, and confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4) — promptly comply with reasonable client requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations included repeated failure to provide filing receipts, acknowledgment receipts, or to respond to clients' repeated inquiries and requests for documents. Anti-pattern: ignoring or substantially delaying responses to simple documentary requests (filing numbers, receipts).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — no dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists numerous examples constituting dishonesty: (i) falsely representing to clients that applications had been filed when they had not; (ii) failing to disclose actual filing dates; (iii) withholding USPTO documents (Confirmation of Micro-Entity Status, authentic Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt, Filing Receipt); (iv) altering an Acknowledgement Receipt (redacting filing date) and providing the altered document to clients to conceal true filing date; (v) misrepresenting that complete client file had been sent when it had not. These are model examples of prohibited deceptive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction — suspension from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and non-patent law for nine (9) months, commencing on the date the Final Order is signed; remains suspended until OED Director grants a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanction imposed for the violations found. Practical consequence: cannot represent clients before the USPTO during suspension unless limited recognition is granted (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to conclude pending matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f), respondent is granted limited recognition for 30 days to conclude work on behalf of clients on any matters pending before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary, narrowly tailored authorization to wrap up existing client matters despite suspension; must be used only to conclude existing matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLE requirement for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, respondent must provide a sworn affidavit/verified declaration and evidence demonstrating successful completion of ten (10) hours of continuing legal education credit on ethics, including at least six (6) hours on law office management for solo or small practitioners and an additional four (4) hours in intellectual property law or ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific quantitative and topical CLE obligations tied to reinstatement. Evidence must be submitted to OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit regarding misrepresentations to other clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must, within 30 days of the Final Order, provide to the OED Director a sworn affidavit or verified declaration attesting that he did not inform any additional client(s) that he had filed patent application(s) on their behalf when he had not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A post-order certification intended to confirm whether similar misrepresentations occurred with other clients; required promptly after entry of order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice management implementation report
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of being reinstated, respondent must provide to the OED Director a written report documenting the efforts he has made during the suspension period to implement a docketing and practice management solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report should demonstrate concrete steps taken to prevent recurrence (software upgrades, workflows, policies). Respondent in this case represented specific improvements (upgraded case management software, CLE seminars, automated workflows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period and support-group reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a probationary period commencing on date of the Final Order and terminating eighteen (18) months after a decision granting a petition for reinstatement; during probation respondent must submit quarterly written reports stating he has continued to attend support groups as recommended by the Texas Lawyers' Assistance Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing monitoring requirement tied to rehabilitation; quarterly reporting cadence specified. Failure to comply may trigger enforcement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement — Order to Show Cause and possible additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes respondent failed to comply with provisions of the Agreement, Final Order, or disciplinary rules during probation, OED Director shall (i) issue an Order to Show Cause, (ii) send it to respondent's last address of record, and (iii) grant respondent 15 days to respond; following consideration, OED Director may request USPTO Director to immediately suspend respondent for up to an additional six (6) months for the violations set forth in the Joint Legal Conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes procedural enforcement steps, timelines (15 days), possible immediate additional suspension (up to 6 months), and evidence/arguments flow to USPTO Director. Practical note: noncompliance triggers expedited disciplinary remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of record in future disciplinary or reconsideration proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, in (1) addressing further complaints or evidence of same/similar misconduct, (2) any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut respondent statements, and/or (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past discipline can be used against practitioner in future matters; a continuing consequence beyond immediate sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the notice text included in the Order describing respondent, the violations (specific CFR provisions), and the sanction(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice is part of disciplinary process; included notice summarizes misconduct (failure to file, failure to communicate, misrepresentations, altered filing receipt) and cites violated rules (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.103, 11.104(a)(3), 11.104(a)(4), 11.804(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has waived all rights to (1) seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, (2) have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and (3) otherwise appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express contractual waiver as part of the Settlement Agreement; effect is immediate finality of the order subject to the agreed-upon reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party is responsible for its own expenses arising from the disciplinary proceeding and settlement implementation.
